questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me there were a couple of crucial factors. First it had to be a English speaking country or a place where majority where able to speak English. The second was that it needed to be a somewhat respected university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There are a bunch of practical stuff you need to do around your arrival and there is a lot of information. It does all work out and people are willing to help or there is easy acces to assistance via office or mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don´t remember receiving additional assistiance upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of campus housing options at NUS. There are Residential Colleges, Halls and some others as well. All are very affordable.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In RC´s and Halls i am pretty sure that there is a mandatory meal plan. Where i lived there were also very well equipped kitchens where you could cook your own food (be carefull of the fire alarm though).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be sure to do everything you can to get student housing! I think that if you do not get any in the initial round, you can apply for round 2 where the chances are pretty high as well if you are willing to live at any place. It makes a big difference for you exchange stay. Also try and apply for the places with a meal plan. You meet so many new people eating in the dining hall and it is just so nice eating together every day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They do a bit of a weird regestration process. When you apply you get approved for some of the 8 courses you had applied for. After that you need to change courses the first couple of weeks of school if you want to change. It is a bit complicated, but it seems like everyone gets the courses they want, except if you study computer science.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think there is an office you can go to or write to, that do a good job at helping.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, in the second round i got all the courses i wanted plus one extra.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be affraid if you do not get your course in the initial application round. If you have the pre requisites the is a high chance you can apply for it and get it when course registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is a bit lower than in Denmark. I think it is because the courses coveres a smaller syllabus.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did not like the style of teaching at NUS at all it seemed very rushed and you did really get anything from the tutorials which a mandatory to participate in for most courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Financial Economics
Evolution of Economic thought and analysis 
Urban Economics
Game Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Game Theory is good because it is a 1:1 of Mikro III
Financial Economics was a good course as well.
Evolution was easy, but the prof was super old and it was a very good course acedemically.
Urban was also quite interesting and different from anything you can take at UCPH

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I do not know if it was unexpected but i did end up traveling a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Singapore can be very expensive but for a student i do not think it is too bad. If you get accomendation on campus you pay very little in rent. Buying food in food stalls around the city is inexpensive as well and activitites are somewhat the same price as in Denmark, maybe a little less. There are a lot of expensive options in Singapore and going out and drinking is quite expensive as well. But overall with the campus accomendation and mealplan i think Singapore is some what affordable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are almost a club or social activites for everything. Some of it is through your accomendation and some of it is through NUS clubs. So no matter what your interest are there is definetly a club or activity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Just do what ever your think is interesting. For the Non team NUS clubs, there is rarely a skill requirement and everyone is welcome. You meet new friends and people at the activities, i would definitly recomend doing a couple. 
The team NUS activites seemed to require a bit of skill and a lot of time since they have a lot of practices through out the week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go explore Singapore it is not as boring as the locals will tell you. There are a bunch of cool events and places to eat and drink around the city.
Other than that go and explore south-east asia. Singapore is a great hub for seeing countries in SEA and with cheap flights as well, or busses and boats if you go to Malaysia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy i think. Singapore is an english speaking country with a lot of international activity, so it a very easy place to live and people are super friendly. It is also a super safe place to be.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Eat at the dining hall, join some of the trips arranged in the exchange group chat and join some of the social activites like sports.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think that eating hot food like rice for breakfast needed a bit of getting used to. Also there is not a big drinking culture which seems strange coming from Denmark. All though it is very nice that not every event contains alcohol.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The safety of Singapore and the extremely polite people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not stress over all the practical stuff in the start/before your exchange. It all works out and there is a lot of help to get.
Do NOT pack heavy clothing. It is hot all the time in singapore, and you only need one sweater for the airconditioned areas like lecture hall. I packed some stuff i never used, like a windbreaking running jacket. 
Try as hard as you can to get student accomendation.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe bring a big travel bag pack. I did a month and a half after backpacking in SEA.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seing an area that is very different from Denmark. It really creates some perspective,

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saying goodbye to all the good friends you made from around the world.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
